subject: HowTo: modify aesthetics of existing ggplot

messages.author: 695eaec5c92d8703
messages.subject: HowTo: modify aesthetics of existing ggplot
parts:
Hi,

I wish to produce versions of a plot that use different columns of my data.frame for x and y.

To that end, I wrote the following function

aesModify.ggplot<-function(p,aes){
    ## PURPOSE: return a new ggplot based on p with modified
    ## aesthetics.
    p$mapping<-modifyList(p$mapping,aes)
    p
}

which I use as follows, after first getting p working with aes(y=y,x=x)

p<-gglot(myData,aes(x=x,y=y), <etc>...) # first, get it the way I want it
ggsave('xy.png',p) # and save it
# now produce versions with modified x,y aesthetics:
ggsave('x2y2.png',aesModify.ggplot(p,aes(y=y2,x=x2))
ggsave('x3y3.png',aesModify.ggplot(p,aes(y=y3,x=x3))
ggsave('x2y3.png',aesModify.ggplot(p,aes(y=y3,x=x2))

It appears to work just fine.

My question is, does anyone see a problem with this approach? 

Or a more direct way to approach it?

I have also used the function to add, for instance, color aesthetics to a plot lacking one.

Thanks for your consideration, and, I hope this approach is useful to others....

~Malcolm

messages.subject: Re: HowTo: modify aesthetics of existing ggplot
parts:
Hi Malcolm,

Thanks for sharing, though it seems like you're basically duplicating
the functionality of ggplot's existing '%+%' operator. Did that not
work for you?

Ben
